IR.rationale: A bear steepening, with intermediate yields rising against policy and the long end rising most, signals a term-premium or repricing shock. Such shocks tend to persist over short horizons and depress bond returns.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads together with weak high-yield returns mark credit stress. That stress triggers flight-to-quality demand for Treasuries and high-grade bonds.

V.rationale: High equity volatility goes with risk aversion and safe-haven flows into government bonds. Since 2000 the stock-bond correlation has been negative.

AP.rationale: Weak equity returns coincide with falling yields because of the negative stock-bond correlation and portfolio rebalancing toward bonds.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to Treasury or investment-grade bond returns.

FX.rationale: A stronger dollar alongside a strengthening yen is the classic risk-off funding-currency pattern. It accompanies safe-haven bond demand.

COM.rationale: Rising oil prices raise inflation expectations and nominal yields, which hurts nominal bond returns. Inflation-linked bonds are partly shielded.

MC.rationale: Rising breakevens without financial stress describe a reflation state. In that state nominal yields drift up and bond returns are poor.

ENDG.rationale: Bond indices show time-series momentum over weeks to months, so strong recent returns carry information about the next period.

IR.rationale: A jump in the 1-year yield relative to Fed Funds signals repricing of the policy path. That raises rate uncertainty and subsequent bond volatility.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads signal stress episodes, which bring large swings in safe-haven flows and in yields.

V.rationale: Elevated equity implied volatility combined with policy uncertainty captures broad uncertainty shocks. These spill over into rate volatility beyond its own persistence.

AP.rationale: Equity selloffs raise cross-asset volatility through leverage, deleveraging and flight-to-quality trades.

ST.rationale: Style factor returns carry little information about future rate volatility.

FX.rationale: Sharp dollar appreciation reflects global tightening or risk-off. Both are associated with more volatile Treasury markets.

COM.rationale: Commodity returns have weak and unstable links to incremental bond volatility. Oil uncertainty is already covered through the V group.

MC.rationale: High measured financial stress precedes and accompanies elevated volatility across fixed-income markets.

ENDG.rationale: Realized variance clusters and mean-reverts nonlinearly, so high recent variance can still carry residual information.

IR.rationale: Bear-steepening repricing, in which yields rise relative to policy and the long end leads, is the state in which sharp bond selloffs develop.

B.rationale: Strong risk-on credit conditions draw flows out of safe assets. They raise the odds of a large Treasury sell-off.

V.rationale: Complacent, low-uncertainty regimes remove the safe-haven bid. Large rate selloffs typically occur with low risk aversion.

AP.rationale: Strong equity gains reflect growth optimism and rotation out of bonds, both of which push yields up.

ST.rationale: There is no clear mechanism linking equity style factors to bond tail losses.

FX.rationale: A weakening yen against the dollar tracks rising US yields and risk-on positioning.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity rallies feed inflation fears and raise the probability of a sharp rise in yields.

MC.rationale: Rising inflation expectations in loose financial conditions describe the reflationary state that produces large nominal bond losses.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent returns signal an ongoing sell-off trend, and momentum raises the chance of a further large loss.

IR.rationale: Falling bill rates and 1-year yields relative to Fed Funds price in easing. That state precedes strong bond rallies.

B.rationale: Credit stress drives flight-to-quality rallies in Treasuries and high-grade bonds.

V.rationale: Spikes in equity fear coincide with safe-haven buying that generates large positive bond returns.

AP.rationale: A global equity sell-off, in both US and emerging markets, signals broad risk-off and strong demand for duration.

ST.rationale: Style factor returns carry little information about bond tail gains.

FX.rationale: Yen strength combined with weakness in the Australian dollar marks carry-trade unwinds in risk-off episodes, when Treasuries rally.

COM.rationale: Falling oil lowers inflation expectations and signals weaker growth, supporting large declines in yields.

MC.rationale: Financial stress together with rising jobless claims signals deteriorating growth and easing expectations, a classic setting for large bond gains.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent returns indicate an ongoing rally, and time-series momentum raises the probability of further large gains.
